page: Microsoft Azure E16ds_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on Microsoft Hyper-V virtualization. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs derived from 8 physical cores on an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at up to 4.2 GHz. The compute topology is backed by 48 KB of L1 data cache per core, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and a shared 260 MB L3 cache. It incorporates vector and matrix acceleration instructions including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX). The instance includes 128 GB of system memory, maintaining an 8 GB per vCPU ratio, alongside a bundled 945 GB local NVMe solid-state drive for high-speed scratch and cache storage.

Benchmark results place the processor in the middle tier for raw compute throughput, achieving a stress-ng multi-core score of 15,971.68 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 10,558.0. Uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 123.39 GB/sec with write throughput at 69.2 GB/sec. The instance delivers strong single-threaded compression performance, recording 31.34 GB/sec in gzip benchmarks. In-memory data structures perform reliably, handling 23.37 million Redis SET operations per second and scoring 8,947.63 in PassMark database operations.

Without discrete GPU acceleration, the platform relies on CPU-bound AMX instructions for inference workloads. It achieves 302.3 tokens per second on lightweight 135M language models, though throughput scales down to 15.78 tokens per second for 7B models. Combining high RAM capacity, fast local NVMe storage, and dedicated vCPUs, the E16ds_v6 is suited for in-memory caching systems, enterprise relational databases, ETL batch pipelines, and memory-intensive analytics.
